correctness.rationale: The exact section formula reduces the problem to the Hessian of \(I_n(a)=\int_0^\infty\prod_j(1+a_j^2t^2)^{-1}dt\). Intrinsic geodesic differentiation gives a rational second-variation integrand. At the sparse point, representation symmetry leaves two tangent eigenspaces and beta integrals give eigenvalues \(-3\) and \((n-8)/n\). At the dense point, the tangent representation is irreducible under permutations and exact integration gives the stated scalar eigenvalues for \(4\le n\le8\). A packaged symbolic checker independently reconstructs and verifies every displayed finite integral and the two candidate-value ratios.

value.rationale: The calculation addresses the local geometry of the two explicit candidates in an open 2026 maximizer conjecture. It shows a genuine bistability window \(n=5,6,7\), proving that the conjectured global change at \(n=6\) is not caused by either candidate immediately losing local stability. The exact eigenvalue \((n-8)/n\) isolates a different, natural quadratic threshold at dimension eight. These are structural facts about a canonical extremal-section problem, not routine recomputation or an arbitrary finite slice.
